triage_candidates.statement: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:1081 -- _handle_door_lease's docstring quotes 'SPINE = Path(os.environ[SPINE_FILE]).resolve()' as scripts/mcp_spine_server.py's existing contract. Commit 4e1f22cb deleted that exact line. Two things are now wrong, the second substantive rather than cosmetic: the expression no longer exists, and after bind-on-open the door's binding can change at runtime, so SPINE_FILE in the hook process's environment is no longer guaranteed to name the spine the door is currently bound to. Found by this rework's blast-radius sweep as the fourth stranded reference; NOT fixed because scripts/hooks/** is fenced to lanes B and C by the g3 handoff's own exclusions.

why_trail.why: The rework is documentation-only by construction, and that shapes everything after it. Blocker 1 is not a map defect: code_map enumerates via git ls-files, so a rebuild run while a new test file is still untracked counts one module short and passes its own guard -- the fix is ordering (stage, then rebuild, then commit), not content. Blocker 2's three references are stranded by 4e1f22cb's own renames: REJECTIONLOG became the _rejectionlog() derivation, and _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle no longer reads ambient SPINE_FILE -- it reads SPINE.parent when bound and falls back to this script's own location when not. Both are docstring claims about mechanism that the mechanism no longer matches.

The sweep found a fourth, and it changes what this rework can deliver. scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:1081 quotes the deleted SPINE assignment as the door's live contract -- a doc reference, so not a stop condition, but inside the lane-B/C fence, so it leaves as a triage candidate rather than a fix. The sweep also measured something the handoff assumed wrongly: map/* is gitignored except INDEX.md and ids.jsonl, so 'regenerate the two map/scripts.mcp_spine_server/ pages' cannot appear in the commit -- those pages are untracked build output. The committable half of blocker 1 is map/INDEX.md alone, which is exactly what the freshness guard reads.

All three in-scope references now name the mechanism that runs. The second was the one that mattered: _spine_open's docstring claimed its repo root came from an ambient SPINE_FILE re-read, but the whole point of the g3 fix is that _primary_checkout_for_lifecycle reads NO environment -- SPINE.parent when bound, this script's own location when not -- and it is precisely the unbound case spine_open exists to serve, so the old sentence contradicted the tool's reason for existing. README:69 also carried a present-tense claim that .mcp.json points at the demo spine, falsified by the same commit emptying the default; corrected in the same sentence as the renamed test. The first attempt at c1 also taught something worth keeping: a blast-radius grep for a removed identifier MUST be word-bounded, or it flags the surviving environment-variable names that embed it.

The rebuild is 3 insertions, 2 deletions to map/INDEX.md -- exactly what the reviewer measured at this commit, which confirms the diagnosis rather than merely agreeing with it: the map was only ever short by the one test module that was still untracked when the last build ran. I also checked whether the trap can fire a third time from what is on disk right now: five untracked .py probe scripts sit under .agent-work/cleanup-a-door/g3-review/, but scripts/code_map/discovery.py:16 excludes the .agent-work/ prefix from the mappable corpus outright, so committing them cannot move the count. The trap needs an untracked .py OUTSIDE .agent-work/, and there is none.

Fully green: 3093 passed, 6 skipped, 1153 subtests, exit 0, after clearing __pycache__. Blocker 1 is closed and closed for the right reason -- the only failure the previous attempt carried was MapTreeFreshness, and it went green from a map rebuild alone, with no test edited and no behaviour touched. That is the evidence that the red was an ordering artefact rather than a defect in 4e1f22cb's substance.

Committed as 359d93df: 3 files, 13 insertions, 9 deletions -- one README paragraph, two docstrings, and the generated map index, which is the whole shape a documentation rework should have. AFTER count on the in-scope surface is ZERO. One stranded reference survives on purpose: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py:1081, inside the lane-B/C fence, carried out as triage candidate tc1 rather than silently fixed or silently dropped.

The delivery is the result file, and it carries the two things a reviewer cannot reconstruct from the diff: that blocker 1 went green from a map rebuild alone -- no test edited, no behaviour touched, which is what proves the previous red was an ordering artefact rather than a defect in 4e1f22cb -- and that the blast-radius sweep found a FOURTH stranded reference the handoff did not know about, sitting inside the lane-B/C fence. That fourth is the one judgment call this gate carried: it is a docstring, so it is not the 'not a doc reference' stop condition, and it is fenced, so fixing it would breach scope. It leaves as triage candidate tc1, named and routed rather than silently fixed or silently dropped.
